DUPLICATE: checked against the 46-row west-operating roster; no other PID represents this same physical CIG system. The 'KM Rockies trio' (P0168 CIG, P0282 WIC, P0270 TransColorado) are confirmed via kindermorgan.com/operations/natural-gas/index as three separately named, separately FERC-tariffed systems under one corporate umbrella — correctly kept as three rows. ATTRIBUTION: Owner='Kinder Morgan' 100% confirmed via Wikipedia ('Coastal merged with El Paso Corp. in 1999, which was bought by Kinder Morgan in 2012') and directly via a kindermorgan.com IR press release specifically about CIG ('El Paso Pipeline Partners Agrees to Acquire Cheyenne Plains Pipeline and Additional Interest in Colorado Interstate Gas Company From El Paso Corporation', May 2012) plus the KM company overview PDF ('Kinder Morgan owns and operates Colorado Interstate Gas (CIG)'). Operator name on the operators/owners tab ('Colorado Interstate Gas Pipeline Co') is a minor label variant of the legal name ('Colorado Interstate Gas Company, L.L.C.' per SEC) — not a defect, just informal sheet naming. SPEC: LengthKnown=6920 km (4,300 mi) and Capacity=5150 MMcf/d are CONFIRMED as genuine network-level totals (this row carries no SegmentName and is the single row for the whole CIG system, so a system-wide source is the correct kind of ref here, not an aggregate-vs-segment defect) via the SEC 10-K ('approximately 4,300 miles of pipeline with a design capacity of 5,150 MMcf/d') and independently via the Kinder Morgan CIG company-overview PDF ('a 4,300 mile pipeline system'), both exact-matching the sheet. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the wiki page's OWN citation for this length figure (cite_note-2) resolves to abarrelfull.wikidot.com, a banned host per standing rules, and does not appear in the harvested wiki_citations.json (correctly filtered out by the harvester) — meaning the sheet had ZERO legitimate support for this number until this pass, despite the number itself being correct. Do not assume any currently-unreffed GEM value is 'probably fine because it's been there a while' — this row's own history shows a correct-but-completely-unsourced number sitting on a banned citation.

validity.researcher_notes: Sheet currently shows StartYear1=2008, StartYearEarliest=2008. This is contradicted by (a) the gem.wiki page's own body text ('Start Year: 1928'), (b) Wikipedia's 'Colorado Interstate Gas' article, which gives a detailed, sourced timeline: formed 1927 as a joint venture of Canadian River Gas Company and CIG, began delivering gas 1 June 1928 (reaching Pueblo 19 June, Denver 22 June 1928), and (c) an independent Texas Panhandle local-history source (Dumas Museum & Art Center, 'CIG Provided Gas for Six States' by Glynda Pflug) that corroborates 1928 construction/service start from a wholly separate origin than Wikipedia. Checked this batch's own convention against sibling rows (P0166, P0219, P0270, P0273, P0282) — StartYear1 in this cohort is used for the original/founding construction year, not the latest expansion year, so 1928 is the convention-consistent value, not 2008. Plausible (not asserted as fact) cause: the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects historical workbook lists a 'CIG High Plains Project' completed 2008-11-15 (216 mi, +900 MMcf/d, 24/30-inch) — a major capacity expansion on this system — and 2008 looks like an expansion-year value that was miscoded into the founding-year field. Two independent sources given (Wikipedia + Dumas Museum, separate origins, neither citing GEM or each other); a third corroborating detail is the wiki's own stated 1928 figure, which is directional support only (not counted as one of the two independents since it is the object under dispute).

validity.researcher_notes: Two distinct defects in the Location cluster, exactly flagging what the task brief called out for this row. (1) StartState/Province = 'Rocky Mountains, Anadarko Basin' — these are geologic/geographic BASIN names, not US states, and don't belong in a State/Province field. SEC 10-K text: 'We deliver natural gas from production areas in the Rocky Mountains and the Anadarko Basin directly to customers in Colorado and Wyoming and indirectly to the Midwest, Southwest, California and the Pacific Northwest.' Wikipedia adds granularity on original construction geography: gas fields in the Texas Panhandle, western Oklahoma, and western Kansas, extending into Wyoming. So the basin names in the current cell are directionally correct (CIG receipts do come from Rockies + Anadarko basin production) but the FIELD should hold states (candidates per the sources: Wyoming, Texas, Oklahoma, Kansas), not basin names — this is a genuine network-level system spanning multiple upstream states, so a single-state answer would itself be an oversimplification; I am not proposing one string because the evidence does not clearly establish which single value (or ordered list) the sheet's convention wants for a multi-state receipt footprint. (2) EndLocation='California' directly contradicts EndState/Province='Colorado' in the same location record — these should describe the same endpoint and currently name two different states. Per the SEC 10-K, California is only an INDIRECT/secondary downstream market (gas moves there via interconnects, not as CIG's own end-of-line), whereas Colorado is the direct, primary delivery area cited repeatedly across all sources (KM overview PDF, SEC 10-K, Wikipedia). This suggests EndLocation='California' is likely simply wrong/should be Colorado-based, but I'm not certifying a specific replacement city/point without route-level data, hence contested value left blank pending a route/GIS pass. Recommend routing to whoever handles P0168's RouteAccuracy/geometry review, since the existing Route [ref] (pipeportal.kindermorgan.com) may itself resolve the exact state list.

Per docs/reference/gem_schema.md, FuelSource must name a single upstream field/plant/facility, never the commodity type ('Natural Gas' would be wrong here, same as the documented Saudi-batch mistake). No single named upstream source is attributable: the SEC 10-K describes receipts from multiple production areas ('the Rocky Mountains and the Anadarko Basin'), and Wikipedia describes the original supply as Texas Panhandle gas fields feeding through the Canadian River Gas Company joint venture. This is a large multi-decade receipt-point network (dozens of interconnects across WY/CO/TX/OK/KS), not a single-field or single-plant-fed line, so no defensible single FuelSource value exists. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than defaulting to a commodity-type or single-field guess.
